record.paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: A universal integration algorithm is meant to perform optimally across multiple smoothness classes rather than being tuned to one specific class. Here tractability concerns how the information complexity n(epsilon,F_d) depends on dimension d and error tolerance epsilon, for example polynomial dependence on d and epsilon^(-1), or strong polynomial dependence on epsilon^(-1) alone. Can universality be developed at the level of tractability as well, so that one studies and characterizes universal algorithms with optimal tractability properties, not only optimal convergence rates?

evidence.quote: If n(epsilon,F_d) is bounded by a polynomial in d and epsilon^{-1} then we say that the problem is polynomially tractable. If n(epsilon,F_d) is bounded by a polynomial in epsilon^{-1} alone ... then we say that the problem is strongly polynomially tractable.

For classical smoothness k > d/2 eran(An,Hkd) \u224d n-k/d-1/2 and e(An,Hkd) \u224d n-k/d. For mixed smoothness k \u2208 N eran(An,Hk,mixd) \u224d n-k-1/2 and e(An,Hk,mixd) \u224d n-k (log n)(d-1)/2. All these orders of convergence are optimal.
Open Problem: Of course one should study universality for tractability questions, not only for the rate of convergence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider multivariate numerical integration on the d-dimensional unit cube. For a class F_d of integrable real-valued functions on [0,1]^d, an algorithm A_n that uses at most n function values produces approximations A_n(f) to the integral I_d(f) = ∫_{[0,1]^d} f(x) dx. The worst-case error of A_n on F_d is

  e(A_n, F_d) = sup{ |I_d(f) − A_n(f)| : f ∈ F_d, ‖f‖_{F_d} ≤ 1 },

and the information complexity is

  n(ε, F_d) = min{ n : there exists A_n with e(A_n, F_d) ≤ ε }.

Tractability notions. The integration problem on the family {F_d}_{d≥1} is called:
 (a) polynomially tractable if there exist constants C, p, q ≥ 0 such that n(ε, F_d) ≤ C d^q ε^{−p} for all d ∈ ℕ and ε ∈ (0,1);
 (b) strongly polynomially tractable if there exist constants C, p ≥ 0 such that n(ε, F_d) ≤ C ε^{−p} for all d ∈ ℕ and ε ∈ (0,1).

Universality. A sequence of algorithms (A_n)_{n≥1} is called universal for a collection 𝒞 = {F_d^{(α)} : α ∈ A} of function classes (indexed by smoothness parameters, weights, or other a priori unknown features α) if, for every α ∈ A, the algorithms (A_n) achieve the optimal order of convergence of e(A_n, F_d^{(α)}) in n as n → ∞, without the algorithm depending on α.

Problem. Develop a theory of universality at the level of tractability rather than only at the level of convergence rate. Specifically:

 1. Formulate a precise notion of a "tractability-universal" algorithm, i.e. a single sequence (A_n) that, for every class F_d^{(α)} in a prescribed collection 𝒞, attains the same (polynomial or strong polynomial) tractability exponents as the best class-specific algorithm tailored to F_d^{(α)}.

 2. Characterize, for natural collections 𝒞 (for example, scales of isotropic Sobolev spaces H^k_d with k > d/2, classes of mixed smoothness H^{k,mix}_d, or weighted Korobov / Hilbert spaces with varying weights), whether such tractability-universal algorithms exist and, when they do, determine the optimal tractability exponents achievable simultaneously across 𝒞.

 3. Provide either explicit constructions of such universal algorithms or prove obstructions showing that tractability-universality must be strictly weaker than class-specific tractability.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) has produced universal algorithms for high-dimensional integration that are simultaneously universal in smoothness and weights and achieve polynomial/strong polynomial tractability in weighted Korobov spaces in both randomized and deterministic settings, addressing aspects of the open problem. However, a general characterization of tractability-universality across broad scales of classes and the constructive determination of optimal tractability exponents remain incomplete, so the broader problem is still partially solved.

status_evidence.title: A simple universal algorithm for high-dimensional integration
status_evidence.snippet: A simple universal algorithm with optimal error rate (independent of dimension) in all weighted Korobov classes in both randomized and deterministic settings.
status_evidence.claim: Recent universal algorithms achieve tractable optimal-order error bounds without prior knowledge of smoothness or weights, partially addressing universality at the tractability level.

status_evidence.title: A simple universal algorithm for high-dimensional integration (Numer. Math.)
status_evidence.snippet: Universality with respect to both smoothness and weights, attaining tractable optimal-order error bounds.
status_evidence.claim: Published 2025 paper provides a constructive universal algorithm with tractability properties.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Algorithms for Numerical Integration: Recent Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem: study universality for tractability questions, not only for the rate of convergence.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as open in the survey, with subsequent partial progress.
